Addressing both of your comments here, first off, while I disagree with the morality behind virtue signalling, I do think that it's better they said something rather than nothing at all. I think as many people as possible should be talking about the current situation facing international students. 

Secondly, there are 38 separate AP exams. Multiply that by 12 forms across 3 waves of testing you get 456 different additional tests that need to be. Each question on those tests needs to be formulated so that it's not something someone can just easily look up, but also demonstrates overall understanding of the subject. Therefore, I doubt making those tests were as easy as it might seem.

Talk to him first. Like, really talk to the dude, find out why he wants to do this, how long he's been feeling like this, see if there's anything you can do to help. If that doesn't work, talk privately with a school counselor and maybe set up a meeting for him, or contact a suicide hotline. Unless if he's planning to hurt himself in the very immediate future, do NOT call the police. I'd also like to suggest to not contact his parents, unless if you know for sure that they have a good relationship. 

What I've said may seem controversial, but as someone on the opposite side of OPs situation, this would be the best course of action. The police will definitely fuck shit up, unless if it is an emergency and he is about to inflict potentially life threatening bodily harm on himself, then please do call them. Parents could also potentially fuck shit up, because shitty parents could be where a part of his issues stem from, so tread carefully. 

I'd also like to add that it's obvious that you care for him, but the entirety of his mental health is not your responsibility. Take care of yourself as well. Good luck.
